meta.title: Trovec Technologies — Engineering Intelligent Digital Futures
meta.description: Trovec Technologies builds AI-powered platforms — anchored by Trovec REIT OS™ and Taskora — across 18 Saudi priority sectors, engineered in Pakistan for Saudi Arabia and the GCC.

hero.title: One technology platform. Eighteen sectors. Not eighteen startups.
hero.shortLede: One shared AI, data and cloud OS for the GCC — engineered in Pakistan. Flagship: Trovec REIT OS™.
hero.lede: Trovec Technologies is a technology platform company — one shared AI, data and cloud operating system powering sector-specific solutions across real estate, finance, infrastructure and public services for the GCC region, engineered from Pakistan. Trovec REIT OS™ is the flagship, currently in design-partner pilots in Pakistan. Every other sector below is labeled honestly by its real stage of development — this is one platform with eighteen surfaces, not eighteen disconnected products.

core.title: One architecture underneath every sector.
core.desc: Every platform below — from LandSmart to a future SafeCity deployment — draws on the same three-layer core, not a separate codebase per sector. That shared core is the argument for why Trovec can credibly cover 18 sectors without becoming 18 disconnected products.
core.stack: AI + DATA + CLOUD + CYBERSECURITY → 18 SECTOR-SPECIFIC PLATFORMS

industries.title: Every sector, honestly staged.
industries.desc: These map to Saudi Arabia's National Privatization Strategy priority sectors. Each card opens to show the proposed Trovec platform, its real development stage, modules, AI capabilities, a sourced market signal where one exists, and Trovec's specific angle.

items.name: Municipalities & Housing
items.one: Urban infrastructure, permits, inspections, waste, GIS.
items.market: Sourced: Saudi real estate market USD 79.1B (2026) → USD 114.0B by 2031, 7.6% CAGR (Mordor Intelligence, Jun 2026). Riyadh faces a 305,000-unit housing gap through 2034.
items.why: Direct extension of LandSmart/BuildSmart, already the most developed Trovec products — this is the flagship sector, not a new build.

items.name: Communications & IT
items.one: Enterprise AI automation, document AI, workflow.
items.market: Sourced: Saudi Arabia declared 2026 the "Year of Artificial Intelligence" under SDAIA, a national digital-transformation priority.
items.why: Treated as a feature layer inside LandSmart and Fiscra, not a standalone product competing with SDAIA-scale national AI initiatives.

items.name: Finance
items.one: Accounting, audit, tax, compliance, CFO services.
items.market: Sourced: SAMA's Open Banking Framework has been live since 2023; ZATCA e-invoicing (Fatoora) integration phases are ongoing and mandatory for applicable businesses.
items.why: Fiscra already exists as working software and is one of two Tier A products — built on the founder's CPA/AFA/audit-governance background.

items.name: Transport & Logistics
items.market: Sourced: Saudi logistics market projected at USD 38.8B by 2026 (5.85% CAGR); Vision 2030 targets 55% of GCC logistics market share (Maersk / Arab News, 2025).
items.why: Deliberately held: no Trovec team or delivered logistics work exists yet, despite genuine Saudi market size.

items.name: Health
items.market: Reliable specific market-size data not gathered for this profile; Vision 2030's broader healthcare transformation program is the directional signal.
items.why: Adjacent to Raymark Healthcare, a separate business line — not a Trovec software product today. Any clinical AI would require formal regulatory validation.

items.name: Riyadh Smart City
items.market: Directional: Riyadh giga-project capital deployment (NEOM, The Line) is well-documented policy direction; no Trovec-specific figure exists.
items.why: A natural LandSmart extension once a Saudi government relationship exists — not pursued speculatively.

reitos.desc: The most developed product in the Trovec ecosystem today. Connects land, development, finance, REIT structuring, investors, and operations in one digital architecture — starting with design-partner RMCs in Pakistan.

trust.text: Saudi real estate market: USD 79.1B (2026) → USD 114.0B by 2031, 7.6% CAGR (Mordor Intelligence, June 2026). Riyadh alone faces a 305,000-unit housing gap through 2034.
Listed Saudi REIT total assets: SAR 31.8B, up 6.7% year-on-year (Q1 2026, Tadawul-reported). REIT market cap ≈ USD 4B across 19 listed funds (S&P Global, 2025).
Every regulatory claim on this page is a public policy signal, not confirmed legal advice — a Saudi lawyer's review is required before any REIT structuring commitment.

taskora.title: Taskora — Pakistan's digital services ecosystem.
taskora.desc: One App. Every Service. Every Need. A Trovec Technologies company, registered as Taskora (Private) Limited under SECP, live at taskora.digital. Unlike the Vision-stage concepts elsewhere on this site, Taskora has its own live website, app download pages, and a detailed five-year feasibility model — it is Trovec's most developed product outside the LandSmart/Fiscra/REIT OS cluster.

features.name: 17 Categories
features.desc: Home Services, Construction & Renovation, Architects & Design, Legal, CAs & Taxation, IT & Software, Tutors & Education, Corporate Services, Facility Management, HR & Recruitment, Digital Marketing, Health & Wellness, Event Management, Logistics & Transport, Security Services, Insurance & Finance, and the Taskora Market Store.

features.name: Trust & verification
features.desc: A 16-point verification standard before any professional can earn on the platform, plus a 310+ document verification library — built to solve the trust problem that keeps most home-services marketplaces small.

features.name: Expansion roadmap
features.desc: Year 1: Islamabad & Rawalpindi. Year 2: Lahore. Year 3: Karachi. Year 4: nationwide across 13 major cities. Year 5+: GCC and international — the same Pakistan-first, GCC-later sequencing used across the rest of the Trovec portfolio.

trust.text: PKR 1.47T+ addressable market, 156M+ population coverage, PKR 81.6B Year-5 revenue target, 3.8x–5.6x expected ROI — figures from Taskora's internal feasibility study.

Taskora's own one-page profile states plainly: "All figures are planning targets from Taskora's internal feasibility model, not audited or achieved results. Prepared for briefing purposes only." This site repeats that caveat rather than dropping it.

Marketplace commissions (40%), corporate contracts (20%), housing society contracts (10%), subscriptions, facility management, featured listings, advertising, training & certification, franchise fees, and future SaaS/analytics.

pakmaweshi.title: PakMaweshi — Pakistan's digital livestock ecosystem.
pakmaweshi.desc: A Trovec Technologies project connecting farmers, traders and buyers through AI-assisted trading, trust, and transparency — livestock marketplace, live auctions, verified traders, veterinary services, insurance, financing, logistics, and meat export/abattoir services, alongside a marketplace store for feed, seed, and equipment. Currently a website prototype; not yet a live transacting marketplace, and no financial or user projections are published here.

compare.title: One core, eighteen verticals — not eighteen separate vendors.
compare.desc: This is Trovec's own positioning argument, not an independently verified market ranking. No competitor names, pricing, or customer counts are claimed here — the comparison is about architectural approach, which is a design choice a prospective customer or partner can evaluate directly.

rows.typical: Separate database per product; no shared identity of a property, entity, or case across tools
rows.trovec: One data core — a property, company, or case carries the same record through LandSmart, Fiscra, and REIT OS

rows.typical: AI bolted on per product, often a thin wrapper on a generic LLM API
rows.trovec: Shared AI layer (document AI, Arabic NLP, predictive analytics) built once, reused across every vertical

rows.typical: Varies by vendor; often absent in early-stage marketplace tools
rows.trovec: Maker/checker and audit-log discipline inherited from Trovec's audit-governance origin, applied platform-wide

rows.typical: Each new sector is a new build, new team, new vendor relationship
rows.trovec: New sectors extend the same core — the 18-sector data model is structured, not hard-coded per page

rows.typical: Often built by generalist software teams entering real estate/finance as a market opportunity
rows.trovec: Built by a team with land-administration and audit-governance experience first, software second

compare.note: This table describes design intent for the Trovec architecture. LandSmart, Fiscra, and Trovec REIT OS currently exist as working software; Taskora has a live website and registered company with a detailed feasibility model but pre-launch marketplace traction; the remaining sectors are concepts built on the same intended core, not yet operational proof of the comparison above.

regional.title: Built against the region's own stated transformation priorities.
regional.desc: Every claim below traces to a public policy source, not an internal projection. Trovec Technologies is an independent company and is not an official government partner, endorsed program participant, or affiliate of any national transformation initiative — the points below describe alignment with publicly stated policy direction, nothing more.

stages.text: 2026 has been publicly framed as a national year of focus on artificial intelligence adoption under the country's data and AI authority, as part of its broader digital-economy priorities.
A New Investment Law (effective Feb 2025) allows 100% foreign ownership in technology, real estate, construction, and logistics via a single investment-ministry registration window.
A Law of Real Estate Ownership and Investment by Non-Saudis is in force from January 2026, opening designated-zone foreign investment in real estate.
A National Privatization Strategy (Jan 2026) names 18 sectors for accelerated PPP investment and faster licensing — the same 18 mapped on this site.
